notes.title: A charge is priced per unit of time
notes.detail: 'late_fee 1% of limit per day' grows with how long the money is outstanding, which prices time rather than a service. For a Shariah-compliant product this has to become a one-off service charge, or a fee tied to a real cost that does not accrue.

region.reading: The gap falls from 36.4% to 15.7% once income is held roughly still, so most of it is income reaching the decision through the policy's income rules rather than region itself. That is a product question - whether this product should serve lower incomes at all - not a defect in the rules.
region.not_a_verdict: This is a measurement, not a compliance opinion. Whether a variable is a legitimate business necessity is a legal question about the product, and nothing here can answer it.

discrimination.reading: Weak separation. A cutoff on this score will cut good and bad alike.
discrimination.caveat: Measured on the 25,584 borrowers who reached the scorecard. The 24,416 stopped by a gate are excluded, which flatters the figure whenever the gates are removing bad borrowers.

cutoff_sweep.what_the_best_threshold_means: The sweep lends at the best threshold (35), so the comparison with the policy's own cutoff is meaningful.
cutoff_sweep.in_sample_warning: The net-maximising threshold of 35 is chosen on the same 25,584 borrowers it is scored against. It is the best cutoff for this cohort's past, and an optimistic estimate for anyone it has not seen. Treat the shape of the curve as the finding, not the argmax.
